text:
sara: quick heads-up — ran a 10m benchmark comparing H100 q8 vs A100 int8 across us-east / us-west / eu-west with edge-fanout enabled. seeing large p95 divergence in eu-west :thinking_face:

mike: paste the numbers?

sara: summary paste: H100-q8
- us-east: p50 46ms, p95 125ms, throughput 230 tok/s
- us-west: p50 50ms, p95 145ms, throughput 215 tok/s
- eu-west: p50 61ms, p95 270ms, throughput 180 tok/s

A100-int8
- us-east: p50 56ms, p95 205ms, throughput 195 tok/s
- us-west: p50 59ms, p95 218ms, throughput 185 tok/s
- eu-west: p50 74ms, p95 395ms, throughput 150 tok/s

mike: whoa eu-west tails are huge. did the run use the same kernel selection across regions? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jia: any routing traces? could be cross-pop hop or proxying.

sara: added a tiny trace sample (internal link): https://dash.redwood/bench/214765
From traces: ~18% of eu-west requests got routed via us-west proxy (SFO) during the run, adding ~100-200ms tail. suspect edge-fanout weights + warmup mismatch.

leo: found this in edge config — we have fallback_fanout: true and weights: {eu-west:0.7, us-west:0.3} but the host resolver sometimes returns the us-west cluster when eu nodes report high load. snippet:
```json
{
  "edge_policy": "geo-preferred",
  "fallback_fanout": true,
  "weights": {"eu-west": 0.7, "us-west": 0.3}
}
```

sara: re-ran a 10m with strict geo pin (no fallback to us-west). results: eu-west H100-q8 -> p50 58ms p95 148ms. so tails drop ~120ms. confirms routing was main contributor.

mike: nice. what about kernel/driver differences? any fallback kernels on eu-west?

sara: yes — at the time eu-west fleet was on driver 525 + fallback kernel (non-fused attn) for some hosts. that increases CPU spin and qkv copy overhead, amplifying tail when requests are proxied. posted kernel map: eu-west had ~12% nodes on fallback.

jia: combine both issues explains A100-int8 worst tails: proxy hop + non-optimized kernel -> p95 spike.

leo: action items:
- disable fallback_fanout for EU runs until weights/health smoothing improved @edge-team (assigned to leo)
- schedule canary of driver 540 + fused-attn kernel on eu-west 10% of hosts (assigned to mike)
- add metric: "cross-pop-hop" tag on traces and alert if >5% (assigned to jia)

sara: i'll re-run the capacity sizing sims after the canary. initial rough calc: with geo-pin, eu-west capacity req drops ~15% because tail reduces and throughput improves.

edge-bot: deploy event: geo-policy update applied to eu-west test namespace by leo at 2147654380 (reacts :white_check_mark:)

mike: thanks — good find. can you attach the raw logs and the small sample script you used?

sara: pasted the script and raw run id in the dashboard link above. quick script for repro:
```bash
# repro load generator (simple)
python tools/loadgen.py --model redwood/h100-q8 --region eu-west --duration 600 --qps 20 --fanout enabled
```

jia: will add the cross-pop tag patch today and set a canary alert.

sara: final note — for planning: when we quote capacity for EU customers, we should incorporate a safety buffer for tail amplification from cross-pop fallback. recommend adding a 20% buffer until driver/kernel fleet parity is near 100%.

leo: noted. ping me if you want me to roll back the change.

mike: ack.
